clue.text: Fire rifle

definitions.meaning: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
to rifle a place is to plunder or ransack it

explanation.surface: A terse order to discharge a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a noun, the gun, but here it is a verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both dismissal from work and plundering a captured town go by the same short word.

clue.text: Something extra mounted to conceal chemical

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the word is set upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a plus is an added extra or bonus
to hide something is to conceal it

explanation.surface: Some additional item has been put up to cover a substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns PLUS upwards to SULP, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound of sulphur with another element is a kind of chemical.

clue.text: Mug, perhaps first to applaud rubbish

indicators.note: the word for applaud is told to come first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
mug is slang for face or mouth, as is trap, so trap is an example of a mug

explanation.surface: Someone with a mug of drink is the first to clap a worthless show.
explanation.walkthrough: Trap and mug are both slang for the mouth or face; 'first to' says the applauding word comes ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, insincere talk aimed at winning applause is nonsense, empty verbiage.

clue.text: Monk to miss having a day in the pub

indicators.note: the two pieces before it are placed inside the word for the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to lack something is to miss it
Fri is the short form of Friday

explanation.surface: A monk wishes he had a day off in the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the missing-plus-day pair inside the pub word. A Black Friar is a Dominican, named for the black cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominican friars wear black mantles, so a member of that order is a type of monk.

clue.text: A sweet dish is served up-a sponge

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the pieces are set upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a dessert of puréed fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A dessert is brought out, along with a sponge cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is served up' turns A + FOOL upwards, giving LOOF A. A FOOL is a British pudding of fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fibrous pod of a gourd is used in the bath as a scrubbing sponge.

clue.text: Study, item on the menu in shopping mall, say

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a course is one part of a meal on a menu

explanation.surface: Someone reads the menu at a restaurant in a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A large open hall where people gather, such as a mall or station foyer, is the example given.

clue.text: Overall positions which are interchangeable in scripture

definitions.text: Overall positions which are interchangeable in scripture

parts.words: Overall positions which are interchangeable in scripture
parts.note: the gospel saying that the leading ones will trail and the trailing ones lead: the two extreme places in a race swap

explanation.surface: A biblical promise that places in a queue will be reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme ends of any ranking are the two positions the Bible says will change places.

clue.text: Endlessly tiresome person will be found in pub — that's natural

indicators.note: the trimmed bore is placed within the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome person

explanation.surface: A dull man is always in the pub, as is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the final E of the tiresome person; 'will be found in' sets what remains within the pub word.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality present from birth is innate, part of one's nature.

clue.text: Rover shows Rex extreme displeasure

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king
anger is strong displeasure

explanation.surface: A dog called Rover is angry with another called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover and Rex both look like dog names; Rover is the definition and Rex gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer through open country, or a Rover Scout, is a ranger.

clue.text: King has to get the hang of being without knight

indicators.note: the letter for knight is removed from the longer word

parts.note: to learn something is to get the hang of it
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A monarch must master life with no knight beside him.
explanation.walkthrough: N for knight comes from chess notation, since K is already the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic old monarch who divided his realm among his daughters.

clue.text: Where mourning birds gathered to make protest

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Who Killed Cock Robin, the birds of the air gathered about the dead bird
a petition or protest signed in a circle so no name heads the list

explanation.surface: Grieving birds flock together to stage a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: the birds stood around Cock Robin.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint with signatures arranged in a ring hides who signed first, a classic form of joint protest.

clue.text: Our Earth'- meant to change, putting off a female with ecological concerns?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase our earth meant are to be altered into a new order
an a is discarded from the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Our planet is meant to change, deterring a woman who cares about the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges OUR EARTH MEANT; 'putting off' means one A from those thirteen letters is left unused.
explanation.definitionFit: The personified natural world is pictured as a mother figure, so she would care for the environment.

clue.text: Is one warm in one's jacket? An awkward situation

definitions.text: Is one warm in one's jacket?
definitions.meaning: a baked spud in its skin, called a jacket in Britain, served hot
a controversial issue nobody wants to handle

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a coat keeps them warm, an embarrassing question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' looks like clothing, but a jacket potato is a baked potato in its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate issue that people pass on quickly, as they would something too hot to hold.

clue.text: It's a wrongful act to take last bit of the cake!

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word the is used

explanation.surface: Grabbing the final slice of cake is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, layered Central European gâteau is a kind of cake.

clue.text: Dispatch note

parts.note: dispatch read as killing: a written order to carry out an execution

explanation.surface: A shipping slip for goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order authorising a hanging is the document sending someone off for good.

clue.text: Relation's friend is an-object of ridicule

parts.note: an aunt is a relation; with the possessive s
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A family member's companion is laughed at.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a fairground game in which people throw sticks at a dummy's head, hence a target of ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set up only to be attacked or mocked, like the fairground dummy.

clue.text: Journalist about to have a drink

parts.note: re means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer is going out for a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer who gathers and files news stories is a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Joined up after action in theatre?

definitions.text: Joined up after action in theatre?

parts.words: Joined up after action in theatre?
parts.note: theatre read as the operating room: a wound is sewn closed after surgery

explanation.surface: Enlisted after a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn together with surgical thread, as an incision is closed after an operation.

clue.text: Royal personage in Berlin — carpet put out

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters of Berlin carpet are thrown into another order

explanation.surface: A royal visitor in Berlin finds the red carpet has been rolled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges BERLIN CARPET.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's German-born consort was a royal personage.

clue.text: Took one's position and collapsed

definitions.meaning: on parade, soldiers take their places in the ranks
a roof or structure that caves in

explanation.surface: Someone took up a stance and then fell down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lining up in formation and caving in are both expressed by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Evil German — no man for one to celebrate?

parts.note: a sin is an evil act

indicators.note: the word for man is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked German is no man to admire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes MAN from GERMAN, leaving GER. The definition is cryptic: someone who celebrates in song.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist may sing praises, celebrating a person or event in song.

clue.text: Girl from the Us lacking a male

indicators.note: the following letters are removed from the country's name

parts.note: the US is America

explanation.surface: A girl from the States who has no boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes A and M from AMERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Pontificate about strike and be extravagant

indicators.note: the word for pontificate goes around the word for strike

parts.note: to spout is to hold forth pompously
to lash is to strike

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off about a walkout while spending freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the pontificating word around the striking word; 'strike' looks like a walkout but means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money lavishly is to be extravagant.

clue.text: Heartless lord keeping in a lady

indicators.note: the trimmed lord holds the following little word within it
with its middle removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel nobleman locks up a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' keeps only the first and last letters of lord; 'keeping' puts the little word inside them, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name stands for a lady.

clue.text: Teasing exercise that might add to someone's stature?

definitions.meaning: making fun of someone by fooling them

definitions.text: exercise that might add to someone's stature?
definitions.meaning: stretching a person's limbs might make them taller

explanation.surface: A joke that a stretching workout could make you taller.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoaxing someone playfully is fooling them, and stretching limbs literally could heighten them.

clue.text: State army occupying university hospital

indicators.note: the word for army is placed inside the other two letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Troops take over a university hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, goes between U and H.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, home to Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Caring type, "Contrary Mary", with name for being a gardener

parts.note: a nurse cares for the sick

indicators.note: being awkward, so the letters of Mary are put in a different order

explanation.surface: The nursery rhyme gardener Mary, quite contrary, is presented as a carer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' rearranges MARY to RYMA. Contrary Mary is the nursery-rhyme gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises plants for sale works as a gardener.

clue.text: Bit in the middle of loaf removed? It's a nail!

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for loaf is singled out
that central letter is taken out

parts.note: bread comes in loaves

explanation.surface: A bite gone from the centre of a loaf turns out to be a nail.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of BREAD, E, is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin wire nail with a tiny head is a kind of nail.
